Query Oracle Database as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__oracle.R
oauth_db_oracle.Rd

Read Oracle data in a Shiny app with each visitor's database permissions. Oracle checks the visitor's access token and maps their identity to database privileges. The helper opens a DBI connection for SQL or dbplyr.

Usage

oauth_db_oracle(
  authorization,
  host,
  service_name,
  driver,
  ...,
  port = 1522L,
  wallet_location = NULL,
  server_cert_dn = NULL,
  authorization_model = c("global", "end_user"),
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

host

One Oracle TCPS listener hostname or IP address.

service_name

Oracle database service name, not a SID or TNS alias.

driver

Registered Oracle ODBC driver name, or its library path when supported by the driver manager. Install a client that supports the database's OAuth integration; newer integrations need a current client.

...

Result options timeout, timezone, timezone_out, bigint, encoding, name_encoding, or interruptible; Oracle ODBC options FBS (fetch buffer size) and DBA ("R" for read-only, "W" for read/write) are also accepted.

port

TCPS listener port. Defaults to 1522; use the port supplied by your administrator, which may differ for self-hosted databases.

wallet_location

Optional Oracle wallet directory for TLS trust or mutual TLS. NULL uses the Oracle client's configured trust store.

server_cert_dn

Optional expected server certificate distinguished name. NULL uses Oracle's hostname matching. Certificate matching is always enabled.

authorization_model

"global" (the default) for a mapped global database user, or "end_user" for an individual Oracle Deep Data Security context. Choose the model configured by your administrator; see Details.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install odbc and Oracle Instant Client's Basic and ODBC packages. The database must trust your provider and audience, map users to database privileges, and use a compatible Oracle client. The Oracle vignette explains the provider-specific setup.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. Connections use encrypted TCPS transport with server certificate checks. Use a wallet when the service requires one.

Authorization models

The "global" model connects as the Oracle global user mapped to the external identity. The helper checks for TOKEN_GLOBAL authentication.

The "end_user" model requires Oracle Deep Data Security direct logon and the jsonlite package. Oracle must establish an end-user context whose issuer, subject and audience match the supplied JWT. Missing or mismatched context is an error; the helper doesn't fall back to a global-schema login.

Keep Entra's /.default consent marker in the client configuration. Use the exact granted database scope in required_scopes.

Connection lifetime

Global-schema connections stay open through token renewal. End-user connections reopen on the next con() call after a token change, so new role claims reach the database. Sign-out, account changes and session end close both types. Reopen broken connections through con().

The Oracle driver reads the token from a temporary file, which is removed after connecting. On Windows, keep R's temporary directory private to the app's operating-system user. For Oracle web APIs, use oauth_db_oracle_ords_api().

See also

vignette("oracle", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_oracle(
  auth$connection,
  host = "database.example.org",
  service_name = "reporting.example.org",
  driver = "Oracle in instantclient_19_30"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT USER AS database_user FROM DUAL")
})
} # }
